name: Provider Hub
description: Provider-neutral connection metadata and bounded live-data read behavior. The buyer supplies provider transport, digest, persistence, credentials, authorization, deployment, and operational controls.
_minModules: The Provider Hub buyer graph starts at the bounded core index and must include its local read adapter and evidence modules. A shorter graph means the portable boundary is incomplete.
_hostFallbacks: Bare or aliased specifiers reached by the buyer graph but supplied by the buyer. Keep empty unless the release gate reports a concrete dependency.
buyerMustSupply: ProviderLiveDataReadTransport — performs buyer-authorized provider reads using buyer-owned credentials and network policy.
ProviderLiveDataDigestPort — produces any required digest without exposing source payloads or credentials.
ProviderConnectionPersistencePort — reads connection metadata from the buyer's own persistence layer.
Credential and vault integration — all provider credentials remain buyer-owned and outside the payload.
Authorization, approval, quota, spend, audit, and deployment controls — the payload does not supply production policy or infrastructure.
notIncluded: Automatic approval, rollout, deployment, or production publication.
A hosted database, vault, network transport, or provider account.
supportedPlatforms: Buyer-selected persistence, vault, and network implementations
Linux and macOS build hosts; no native modules

upgradeCompatibility.policy: Within 1.x the buyer-facing interfaces are additive only.
upgradeCompatibility.ledgerSchema: The payload owns no datastore schema.
upgradeCompatibility.rollback: The payload holds no state and can be replaced by restoring the previous verified archive.

knownLimitations: The release candidate validates packaging and integrity only; it is not evidence of buyer deployment acceptance.
Live data requires a buyer-supplied transport and buyer-owned provider authorization.
Provider writes, credential transfer, automatic rollout, and production execution remain disabled.

acceptance.how: Import the entry point in a clean buyer environment, create redacted connection metadata, and exercise live-data reads only through buyer-supplied test doubles before production wiring.
acceptance.guarantee: The payload contains no credentials and performs no provider mutation, deployment, or automatic production action.
acceptance.evidence: Keep the independently verified manifest, SHA-256 results, clean extraction result, and buyer test record.
